items: Caption: Contextual rewards, clues, and emotional residue.
Gmgoal: Make searches reveal who people were, not just what they carried.

Gmnotes: Hexmart Pocket Ward™ (cracked): No real ward effect; failed consumer protection charm. The driver trusted cheap protection and it failed. Stride Salve: Clear 1 Stress or move at Far without a roll once. Common frontier aid for exhausted couriers. Grindstone Vial: Next damage roll adds +1d6. Lark-Moth Lantern: Soft light; once/rest ask GM one question about immediate area, no roll. Bramble-Cutter's Hook: 1d6 physical tool-knife; advantage on Finesse or Strength rolls to cut ropes, vines, snares, or free someone Restrained by brambles. Compliance Stamp (forged): Once, auto-pass bureaucratic/checkpoint gate without rolling; risky if inspected. Firstmoss Poultice: Tend to Wounds: clear 1d4+1 HP outside a rest. Bag of Mixed Chits: Currency. Whetcord: Once, reroll a damage die and keep the higher. Tinker's Kit, Used: Advantage on Finesse rolls to pick locks, disarm simple traps, or jury-rig. Soul-Quiet Charm: One use: clear 1 Stress caused by fear, memory, or wraith backlash, or gain advantage on a Presence or Knowledge roll to recover from a Soul-Audit Wraith module effect. Adaptation, not official Daggerheart. Strixwolf-Down Cloak: Once/rest, advantage on Agility roll to move...
Playertakeaway: GM-only loot reference; reveal only the reward or clue the PCs actually find.
Storytakeaway: Rewards should say something about the world, not just add inventory.
Mechanictakeaway: Use listed effects when present; otherwise treat loot as story evidence or color.
